novel_features.name: Schema grep
novel_features.description: Find any form, field, or subform on your tenant by name fragment, instantly and offline.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the parsed-$metadata SQLite cache this CLI builds; the raw EDMX is >10MB and no API endpoint searches it.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Reach for this before any entity call on an unfamiliar tenant — field names differ per install and guessing burns the 100/min rate cap.

novel_features.name: Schema snapshot diff
novel_features.description: Snapshot your tenant's schema and see exactly which forms and fields changed after an upgrade or customization.
novel_features.rationale: Requires named schema snapshots stored locally in SQLite — nothing in the API reports schema drift.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Run after tenant upgrades to find silent field changes before integrations start failing with 400s.

novel_features.name: License probe
novel_features.description: Discover which forms are actually API-enabled on this tenant instead of finding out via 400 errors.
novel_features.rationale: No endpoint reports API licensing; this runs throttled $top=1 probes and caches per-tenant verdicts locally.
novel_features.why_it_matters: "API Cannot Be Run for This Form" is the most common real-world Priority API failure; probe once, know forever.

novel_features.name: Batch journal + resume
novel_features.description: Re-run only the failed operations from a partially-failed $batch — Priority batches have no rollback.
novel_features.rationale: Requires the per-operation SQLite journal that batch load writes; the API itself cannot tell you what landed.
novel_features.why_it_matters: After a half-failed bulk load, this is the difference between surgical recovery and manually diffing response JSON.

novel_features.name: Sync reconcile
novel_features.description: Verify your local mirror matches the live tenant using windowed probes — the API has no $count.
novel_features.rationale: Requires comparing local SQLite row counts against live windowed probes; no single API call can verify sync completeness.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Answers "did last night's sync actually get everything" without a full re-pull.

novel_features.name: Shortage (ATP)
novel_features.description: See which parts will run out given the open order book — open demand vs on-hand stock, optionally netting inbound POs.
novel_features.rationale: Requires a three-table local join (order lines, parts, purchase orders) that exists in no Priority screen and no single OData call.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Replaces the weekly Excel VLOOKUP between order lines and stock; sync orders with --resource-param "orders:$expand=ORDERITEMS_SUBFORM" first, and expect on_hand null when the tenant exposes no balance fields.

novel_features.name: Customer 360
novel_features.description: One command for a customer's whole picture: invoiced totals, age buckets by invoice date, open orders, recent invoices.
novel_features.rationale: Collapses four separate live lookups into one local join over synced customers, invoices, and orders.
novel_features.why_it_matters: The pre-collections-call briefing, at terminal speed, without burning the rate cap.

narrative.headline: The entire Priority REST API — every form, subform, batch, and attachment — plus offline sync, schema intelligence, and throttle-safe bulk operations no other Priority tool has.
narrative.value_prop: Priority exposes every ERP screen as an OData entity, but ships no CLI and no official SDK. This CLI covers the full surface — generic CRUD on any form, OData query options, $batch, attachments, text subforms, metadata — and then goes beyond it: a local SQLite mirror with full-text search, per-tenant schema intelligence ('forms search', 'forms licensed'), and batch journaling with resume ('batch resume'). A built-in adaptive limiter keeps every command under Priority's 100-requests-per-minute fair-use cap.
narrative.auth_narrative: Priority instances are per-tenant: set PRIORITY_BASE_URL to your service root (https://<server>/odata/Priority/<tabula.ini>/<company>). Authenticate with Basic credentials via PRIORITY_API_USERNAME and PRIORITY_API_PASSWORD — the username is the 'API User Name' from the Personnel File form, not your login name. For server-to-server automation, use a Personal Access Token (REST Interface Access Tokens form): set PRIORITY_API_USERNAME to the token and PRIORITY_API_PASSWORD to the literal string PAT. The default base URL points at Priority's official public sandbox (user apidemo, password 123, read-only).

quickstart.comment: Verify configuration safely; drop --dry-run to test live connectivity
Query any form with OData options — this is the generic surface that covers the whole API
Build the local mirror that powers offline search and analytics
Full-text search the mirror without burning the 100/min rate cap
One-command customer 360: invoiced totals, age buckets, open orders, recent invoices

troubleshoots.fix: You hit Priority's fair-use cap (100 calls/min/user). The built-in limiter backs off automatically; for bulk work use 'batch load' (journaled, 100 ops per request) or lower 'sync --max-pages'.

troubleshoots.symptom: 400 with 'API Cannot Be Run for This Form'
troubleshoots.fix: The form is not API-licensed on your tenant. Run 'priority-pp-cli forms licensed --forms <FORM>' to map which forms are enabled, then ask your Priority admin to license the rest.

troubleshoots.symptom: 404 Not Found on an entity that exists in the UI
troubleshoots.fix: Form and field names are case-sensitive UPPERCASE (ORDERS, not orders). Run 'priority-pp-cli forms search <name>' to find the exact form name on your tenant.

troubleshoots.symptom: $since returns an error on some entities
troubleshoots.fix: $since only works on entities with BPM (business process management) applied. Use a $filter on a date field instead for non-BPM forms.

troubleshoots.symptom: Cannot address a record with a composite key
troubleshoots.fix: Pass the full key spec: priority-pp-cli entity get AINVOICES "IVNUM='T9696',IVTYPE='A',DEBIT='D'".

narrative.when_to_use: Use this CLI whenever an agent or script needs Priority ERP data or writes: querying any form with OData options, creating or amending business documents (orders, invoices) including subform lines, bulk loads via $batch, attachment and text handling, and tenant schema discovery. The local mirror makes it the right choice for repeated lookups, search, aging/debtor/shortage analytics, and any workflow that would otherwise burn the 100-requests-per-minute cap.
anti_triggers: Automating the Priority web UI or form engine flows (use priority-web-sdk — this CLI speaks the OData REST API only)
Running Priority procedures or printing reports (the OData REST API does not expose procedure execution)
Administering users, licenses, or tenant configuration (not exposed via the REST API)
Real-time event push — the API has no streaming; use 'priority-pp-cli tail' for near-real-time polling

recipes.title: Order drill-down with narrowed agent output
recipes.explanation: Orders with expanded line items return tens of KB; --select with dotted paths keeps only what the agent needs.

recipes.title: Find tenant-custom fields before writing
recipes.explanation: Per-install custom fields (ORGT_* prefixes) are invisible in the docs; grep the cached schema before building a payload.

recipes.title: Bulk load with surgical recovery
recipes.explanation: Preview a journaled $batch load; drop --dry-run to execute, and 'batch resume <id>' re-runs only failed operations.

recipes.title: Monday collections review
recipes.explanation: Book-wide AR aging buckets from the local mirror; follow with 'debtors' for the ranked call list.

recipes.title: Raw OData escape hatch
recipes.explanation: Anything the API can express that no typed command covers — with auth and throttling still handled for you.
